1.0.0.en: "The book of the generation": that is, a genealogical table, taken from the genealogical tables that the Jews took care to preserve while awaiting the coming Messiah. These tables were lost when Jerusalem was destroyed in AD 70 at the hand of Titus, the Roman commander. God ordained their concern for these tables so that this would be proof that Christ is the son of David, so that they might believe in Him.

1.0.1.en: There are two genealogical tables of Christ in the Holy Bible. One is in Luke (Lk 3:23-38), who addresses the Gentiles, so he records the legal lineage, that is, the males whom the Law regards as fathers: if a man died without having children, his brother would marry his wife, and the offspring would be reckoned to the one who died (Deut 25:5-6). Some of the sons mentioned are therefore sons by adoption, to proclaim to the Gentiles that they are sons by adoption and have salvation just like the Jews. As for Matthew (Mt 1:2-17), because he addresses the Jews, he records the natural fathers, because they are the people of God, descended in sequence from their natural fathers, that is, the Jews.

1.0.2.en: So we see that Joseph, the betrothed of Mary, has a legal father, Heli, who is mentioned in Luke, who died without having children.

1.0.3.en: As for Jacob, who is mentioned in Matthew, he is his natural father, as St. Severus of Antioch says. As for John (Jn 1:1-2), he wrote His divine lineage.

1.0.4.en: "Jesus Christ": Jesus is the human name of Christ, and its meaning is Savior.

1.0.5.en: As for Christ, it means the One anointed by God for this service, that is, the redemption of mankind. In the Old Testament the prophet, the priest and the king were anointed, and these three were united in Christ; and the anointed one has authority from God to carry out his work.

1.0.6.en: "The son of David, the son of Abraham": He is the son of David the king, as the prophecies mentioned (Isa 9:7), and the son of Abraham, as God promised him (Gen 22:18).

1.0.7.en: It was known to all the Jews that the awaited Messiah would come from the seed of David and Abraham.

1.1.0.en: A) It is noticed in this series that the genealogy descends from Abraham to Jesus, since Christ bears the sins of mankind, redeems us and saves us, because this series carries many sinners, such as Rahab the harlot, Tamar who put on the garment of a harlot, and the wife of Uriah, with whom David committed adultery. Whereas St. Luke ascends in his genealogy from Jesus to Adam, raising all mankind to God, the Father of Adam, because Luke addresses the Gentiles.

1.1.1.en: B) Matthew speaks in the genealogy of the natural fathers of Jesus, who were begotten by physical procreation, whereas Luke mentions the legal fathers.

1.1.2.en: C) The genealogy ends with Joseph and not the Virgin, although Joseph did not physically beget Christ. But the Jews recognize only men in genealogies, so, to protect Christ before Jewish society, Joseph was regarded as His father, as the angel informed him (vv. 20-21).

1.1.3.en: At the same time, the Virgin too is of the seed of David, for when they wanted to send her out of the Temple on reaching the age of twelve, they brought men from the seed of David, and God chose Joseph to be her betrothed.

1.1.4.en: There is another opinion, which is that Luke recorded the lineage of Christ through Mary His mother, so he mentions Heli, who is the father of Mary and is also called Joachim, and he attributes Joseph's lineage to him; and it was known among the Jews that a man could be reckoned to his father-in-law.

1.1.5.en: In any case, the two genealogical tables of Christ in the Gospels of Matthew and Luke were among the tables accepted by the Jews, as is proved by their not objecting to them.

1.1.6.en: D) Among the grandmothers of Christ were Rahab the Canaanite and Ruth the Moabitess, so that Christ might proclaim that He came for the salvation of the whole world, Jews and Gentiles.

1.1.7.en: E) Matthew the Evangelist mentions that the genealogy is divided into three parts, each part of 14 generations. It seems that the Jews tended to use certain numbers for blessing, such as the number 7, and the number 14 is double the number 7.

1.1.8.en: It seems that this series was written down and known among the Jews, for although it has abbreviations, these tables omitted names, such as King Joram, who did not beget Uzziah but begot Ahaziah, who begot Joash, and Joash begot Amaziah, and Amaziah begot Uzziah.

1.1.9.en: So Matthew abridged these names to reach his goal, which is that the Messiah is of the seed of David and Abraham. And although the first series began with Abraham and reached David the great, the second series descends through those who were in captivity because of the sins of the people, and then the third series rises to reach Jesus, the Savior of the whole world.

1.1.10.en: F) The series of Matthew differs from that of Luke, and this confirms that neither of them looked at the other's book, but each wrote it truthfully by inspiration of the Holy Spirit, to inform us of more details about Christ.

1.1.11.en: If Christ was not ashamed to mention His wicked and Gentile ancestors, then we should honor our fathers and relatives, even if their social standing was low, and appreciate their labors and virtues. Nor should we forget that our most important lineage is to Christ and the Church in which we were born through Baptism, so we have confidence in ourselves and are distinguished from those around us by this great grace, and we do not despise anyone of lowly lineage, for he may be better than we are in the sight of God and will have a greater place in heaven. Let us respect and honor every person and look for his virtues so that we may benefit from them.

1.2.s.en: (2) Joseph's first dream and the Mother of Christ

1.2.0.en: "Espoused": that is, joined to a man, so that when she bore Jesus He would be ascribed to a man, namely Joseph, before Jewish society, and she would not be counted an adulteress.

1.2.1.en: Betrothal among the Jews meant a marriage contract, and the betrothed woman was called the wife of the betrothed; but after the period of betrothal, physical union took place, as happens now among our Muslim brothers in the signing of the contract and then the consummation. So after the betrothal was completed, when Joseph received Mary from the Temple, he took her to his house and kept her as a betrothed in purity and did not approach her. But he was surprised to find her with child before the marriage was completed, and he was disturbed, and was perplexed between her innocence and the pregnancy that he saw with his own eyes. And Matthew's saying, "before they came together," that is, during the betrothal, in no way means that they came together afterward, for the Virgin is ever-virgin.

1.3.0.en: It was open to Joseph to hand Mary over to the priests so that they would stone her, or to divorce her and send her out of his house secretly, without scandal. And because he was righteous, he wanted to cover for her and let her go without punishment, so that he would not be a partner in the crime of concealing a sin.

1.3.1.en: The more you love God, the more your love appears toward those around you, even if they are mistaken in your sight; so do not condemn them but cover for them, because "love covereth all sins" (Prov 10:12). And as God covers for you, be merciful to others as well.

1.4.0.en: "Joseph, thou son of David": the angel reminds him of his lineage from David, from whom Christ would come.

1.4.1.en: Because Joseph was a righteous man who quickly understood the revelations of God, an angel appeared to him in a dream and informed him of the truth of the Virgin's conception, that it was of the Holy Spirit and not of man, and encouraged him to take her, that is, to keep her in his house, and to look after her and the One to be born; indeed he told him the name of the One to be born, which is Jesus, meaning Savior, because He saves those who believe in Him from their sins.

1.4.2.en: "He shall save his people from their sins": He is a Savior, not from the Roman occupation as the Jews thought, but a spiritual Savior who lifts them out of their sins so that they may live in righteousness.

1.4.3.en: If you are perplexed between two difficult matters, God is able to guide you to the better solution, as the angel guided Joseph, if you pray to Him.

1.5.0.en: Matthew reminds us of the prophecy of Isaiah (Isa 7:14); this is the word of Matthew and not of the angel, as he tells us of the conception of the virgin, who is Mary, and explains to us the meaning of "Emmanuel", that is, that God becomes incarnate and becomes man among us, and redeems us, and is with us and dwells in us.

1.5.1.en: If God proclaims His name Emmanuel, that is, God with us, then in His love He wants to draw near to us and be with us in order to save us from all our sins and troubles.

1.6.0.en: Joseph's righteousness appears in his obedience to God, for he rejected his first idea, which was to send her out of his house, and even declared his responsibility for her, and believed the word of God although it is beyond the grasp of the mind.

1.7.0.en: Joseph took care of the Virgin until she bore the Child, and he called Him Jesus as the angel had declared, and he continued to care for her throughout his life.

1.7.1.en: And when Matthew mentions that he "knew her not till she had brought forth", it does not mean that he knew her after that, but that he did not approach her physically and cared for her as a father. The word "till" comes with this meaning in many places in the Holy Bible, as the Psalm says: "So our eyes wait upon the LORD our God, until that he have mercy upon us" (Ps 123:2); it does not mean that after He has mercy on us we do not lift our eyes toward Him.

1.7.2.en: Likewise, when Noah sent forth the raven from the ark, the Holy Bible says: "which went forth to and fro, until the waters were dried up from off the earth" (Gen 8:7); the word "until" does not mean that after the earth dried the raven returned to the ark, but that it remained on the earth.

1.7.3.en: And Jesus is described as "firstborn", not because the Virgin bore other sons after Him, but because the first one born is called firstborn even if no one is born after him.

1.7.4.en: And by logical deduction, it is impossible for righteous Joseph, whom God chose for this holy task, to defile the womb that the Holy Spirit sanctified.

1.7.5.en: The visit of the Magi, the flight to Egypt and the return to Nazareth

2.0.0.en: The Magi were the astrologers who were concerned with the study of medicine and astronomy; they were scholars in their country and were also regarded as priests, and they had a great standing that their gifts show. They came from the east, most likely from Persia or Iraq. Their number is not mentioned, but at least three of them were prominent, and they may have had a large following; and they had heard prophecies from their forefathers about the appearance of a star that points to the birth of a great king. Balaam the son of Beor the prophet said this, and he was from the east where they live: "I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not nigh: there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel, and shall smite the corners of Moab, and destroy all the children of Sheth" (Num 24:17). They may also have understood this from Daniel, who was chief of the Magi, from his prophecy about the birth of Christ: "Know therefore and understand, that from the going forth of the commandment to restore and to build Jerusalem unto the Messiah the Prince shall be seven weeks, and threescore and two weeks: the street shall be built again, and the wall, even in troublous times" (Dan 9:25).

2.0.1.en: The star that they saw was not an ordinary star; it was either an angel who appeared in the form of a star, or a special spiritual star that God sent, and this appears from the following:

2.0.2.en: A) The stars move from west to east, but this one moved from east to west.

2.0.3.en: B) This star appeared in the daytime while the sun was bright, and not only at night.

2.0.4.en: C) It sometimes appeared and sometimes disappeared (as happened when they asked Herod).

2.0.5.en: D) It traveled high in the sky, then came down over a lowly house where Christ was born.

2.0.6.en: So when the star brought them from the east as far as Jerusalem, they were certain of the prophecies, and that He was the king of the Jews, and they supposed that He would be born in the royal palace, so they asked those in the palace.

2.1.0.en: This Herod is the one called Herod the Great. He was of Edomite origin, an intruder upon the Jews, and he had seized the kingship by force. He was marked by violence: he killed his wife and some of his sons, and he was at that time seventy years old, so he feared the new King. The news spread in the palace and throughout Jerusalem, and they were troubled and bewildered as to what surrounded the birth of the new King, and whether conflicts might arise between Him and Herod!

2.1.1.en: And this Herod is the father of Herod Antipas who killed John the Baptist, and the grandfather of the Herod who killed James the son of Zebedee and imprisoned Peter.

2.2.0.en: Herod understood that they were speaking about the awaited Messiah, and he feared that the kingdom would be taken from him, so he gathered the chief priests, that is, the present high priest and the former high priests, and all the heads of the priestly divisions, and the scribes of the Law who studied it, to inform him where Christ was to be born so that he could kill Him.

2.2.1.en: However great a person's greatness and authority, he cannot keep his peace as long as he is in sin, far from God, for peace is enjoyed only by the children of God.

2.3.0.en: "Bethlehem": it is a small village southwest of Jerusalem, about 8 km away from it, and it is also called Ephratah (Mic 5:2), or the city of David because he was born in it (Lk 2:4), and Micah the prophet prophesied about it (Mic 5:2). It is in Judea, to distinguish it from another city called Bethlehem in Galilee, and it is clear from the prophecy that it was small and lowly, but it became very great through the birth of Christ in it.

2.3.1.en: Note how the priests and their chiefs did not take care to search for the awaited Messiah, of whom the prophets had spoken and to whom the types pointed, because they were occupied with their positions and their wealth. Whereas the Gentiles, those far from Him, in the form of the Magi traveling from a distant land, searched for Him, so that the Holy Bible might confirm that Christ came for the salvation of the whole world, and He draws every person to Himself in the way that suits him (the Jews by the prophecies, and the Magi by the star because they were astronomers); what matters is that a person respond to the voice of God.

2.3.2.en: So however weak or lowly you are, you are turned into the greatest of people by Christ's dwelling in your heart.

2.4.0.en: After Herod learned the place of Christ's birth, he asked the Magi about the time when the star appeared to them in their country, and he calculated the time until their arrival from Persia in Judea, and it was more than a year, in order to know the age of the new King.

2.4.1.en: "Privily": because he felt his own wickedness, as he intended to kill Christ, so that his plan to kill the children of Bethlehem, with which he would take the Jews by surprise, would not be revealed.

2.5.0.en: Herod hid the cruelty in his heart and his desire to kill the new King, and showed himself in innocence to the Magi, as though he wished to worship Him as they did, so he asked them to find out the place with care and then tell him. It seems that, in his agitation, he did not send anyone after them to learn the place of the Child.

2.6.0.en: The Magi relied on their own reasoning, so they asked in the royal palace where they supposed the new King would be born, and no one guided them; then they went out and found that the star had disappeared from them. And after they failed to learn His place, the divine star appeared to them and they rejoiced greatly, and it led them to Bethlehem and then to the house in which Christ was born.

2.6.1.en: Hold fast to God's commandments so that they may guide you on the path of your life, and likewise the guidance of your father of confession above all your thoughts and reasoning, lest you stray from Christ.

2.6.2.en: So do not be hindered by the cares of the world and its reasoning from your goal, which is the love of God, and the measure of your holding fast to God's commandments will continue to guide you; but if you neglect it you will be perplexed and ask: how can I hear the voice of God?

2.7.0.en: When they saw the child Jesus with His mother the Virgin and Joseph the carpenter, they felt great reverence, and they worshiped Him with hearts full of joy, then presented to Him their gifts, which were gold, frankincense and myrrh, and these point to the offices of Christ: gold because He is King; frankincense, that is, incense, because He is a Priest by the sacrifice of Himself on the Cross; and myrrh is a reference to His sufferings and death. Perhaps these gifts were a help to the Holy Family in some of the costs of the journey to Egypt.

2.7.1.en: The greatness of the Magi's faith in Christ appears here, that He was in a lowly form; and note also the Jews' lack of concern to glorify their King, whereas they believed according to God's guidance to them by the star.

2.8.0.en: The Magi did not understand the wicked intention of Herod, but God, after their visit to Christ, informed them in a dream not to return to Herod because he was wicked, and guided them to another way by which they returned to their country. It seems that this dream came to them right after seeing Christ so that they might hasten their departure to their country, before Herod noticed and carried out his plan to kill the children of Bethlehem.

2.8.1.en: If you have enjoyed sitting with Christ, do not return to wicked Herod, that is, your former evils, but return to your first homeland, which is Paradise where Adam was created of old, that is, lift your heart to heaven, continuing in a spiritual relationship with God.

2.9.0.en: The Magi told the Holy Family what God had said to them in the dream, and they understood that Herod was seeking Jesus to harm Him, but they were not troubled, and waited for God's guidance. Then God's care for them and His mocking of wicked Herod appeared: the angel of God appeared in a dream to Joseph for the second time and asked him to take the child Jesus and His mother Mary and flee with them to Egypt, and to be there until he told him.

2.9.1.en: And Egypt is the nearest place to Judea and is not under the authority of Herod.

2.9.2.en: In this, God declares to us fundamental matters in our spiritual walk, which are:

2.9.3.en: A) The necessity of enduring sufferings so that a person may be proved; how hard it was for old Joseph, young Mary and the child Jesus to bear the hardships of travel and of living in a foreign country.

2.9.4.en: B) The confirmation of Christ's Incarnation, and His bearing all the suffering of mankind from His childhood, not using the power of His divinity to ease Himself.

2.9.5.en: C) Not resisting evil but fleeing from it.

2.9.6.en: D) The blessing of Egypt, that it might be a center of spiritual work through the generations by its scholars, its monks and its saints.

2.10.0.en: Joseph the carpenter obeyed the angel's word, not excusing himself because of his old age, or the smallness of the Child, or his not knowing Egypt, and he arose by night to travel to it.

2.10.1.en: "By night": most likely on the very night in which he saw the dream, to hurry in the flight before Herod's plan was carried out; and because he was a stranger he did not have many belongings that needed preparing for the journey, and likewise no one paid attention to him, for he was not from the people of the place.

2.11.0.en: The Holy Family moved to Egypt, passed through many places and blessed them, and stayed there about two years until Herod died, and by this the prophecy of Hosea the prophet was fulfilled about the Messiah's return to the land of Israel: "Out of Egypt have I called my son" (Hos 11:1). This prophecy was about the exodus of the children of Israel from Egypt, and also about the return of Christ from Egypt to the land of the Jews.

2.12.s.en: (4) The slaughter of the children of Bethlehem

2.12.0.en: Herod was greatly enraged because of the Magi's disobedience to him and regarded it as a great insult, and his fear of the new King increased, so in hardness of heart he decided to kill all the children of Bethlehem, among whom was the new King. And to make sure of killing Him, he asked the soldiers to surround the place, so that no one would escape from all the borders (boundaries) of Bethlehem.

2.12.1.en: And according to his expectation of the age of the new King, that He would be about a year old or more, he asked that all the children up to the age of two years be killed, to make sure of getting rid of Him, lest the soldiers err in estimating the children's ages; and he likewise ordered the killing of all those around Bethlehem, and also those older than the age of the Child, so that he would have done away with Him, and this shows Herod's brutality.

2.13.0.en: By this the prophecy of Jeremiah, referred to previously in (v. 8), was fulfilled, which expresses what happened during the captivity, and also what happened in the massacre of Bethlehem, where the news spread throughout Jerusalem and its surroundings, since the city of Ramah lies north of Jerusalem, and they heard the weeping and wailing of the Jewish mothers (who are symbolized by Rachel) for the loss of their children. Also Rachel, the wife of Jacob, who is buried in Bethlehem, wept first for those who were killed in the days of the Babylonian captivity, and weeps also for the children killed in the days of Herod. All this is a symbol of the grief that prevailed, not only in Bethlehem but in all the lands surrounding Jerusalem.

2.13.1.en: Hardness of heart makes a person not feel those around him, so he wrongs them while he is absorbed in achieving his own aims. May you put yourself in the place of others so that you feel for them, and may your achieving your aims not be at the expense of people's comfort, but may you seek their comfort before your own, as Christ did when He died for our redemption and salvation.

2.14.0.en: After the Holy Family had stayed about two years in Egypt, waiting for God to permit them to return to the land of Israel, the angel appeared to Joseph for the third time and informed him of the death of Herod and of his son Antipater, who had wanted to kill Jesus (for Herod killed his son five days before he died, after he had completed 37 years in the kingship, and that was in 4 BC). And the angel commanded Joseph to return.

2.15.0.en: Joseph obeyed, and did not ask to remain in Egypt, excusing himself because of his old age or to keep away from the wicked in Judea, for the virtue of obedience is above all reasoning, so that God may lead the life of the one who obeys Him.

2.16.0.en: When Joseph reached the borders of the land of Israel, he heard that Archelaus, the son of Herod, had reigned in his place, and he was known for cruelty like his father, so he feared to return to Bethlehem near Jerusalem, where he had supposed it to be a suitable place for Christ to live, near the Temple and the priests of the Jews. And he asked God what to do. Then he was "warned of God in a dream", perhaps by an angel as in the previous times, to go to Galilee, which is in the north of the land of Israel, where Herod Antipas, the brother of Archelaus, reigned, and there were problems between them, in addition to his being gentle.

2.17.0.en: When he reached Galilee, he went to the city of Nazareth, where he had lived at first, for it was his original home, and by this the prophecies of the prophets were fulfilled that He would be called a Nazarene.

2.17.1.en: And the word "Nazareth" means a branch, and Isaiah, Jeremiah and Zechariah prophesied that Christ would be called the Branch (Isa 11:1-2; Jer 33:15; Zech 3:8), and this is the fifth time that St. Matthew cites the prophecies.

2.17.2.en: And Jesus lived in Nazareth about 28 years until He reached the age of thirty, and He worked with Joseph the carpenter in carpentry. Not much is recorded about this period except that He was obedient to His mother and Joseph, and was growing in stature and grace, and visited Jerusalem at the feasts to fulfill the worship according to the Law. God leads your life, so do not be troubled by the wicked however much they threaten you, for Herod and his son Antipater have died, and as for Archelaus, God took His Christ away from him when He settled in Galilee. The power of the wicked is worthless before God, so walk in calm and reassurance, occupied with God, and He protects you from every evil.

2.17.3.en: E The preaching of the Baptist and his baptism of Christ
